newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE Oasis Leasing says IPO heavily oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: UAE Oasis Leasing says IPO heavily oversubscribed.

text.p: Oasis International Leasing Co said its initial public offering was five times oversubscribed, attracting a total of 1.4 billion dirhams ($409 million) from investors, the official WAM news agency said.
Speaking at a news conference, head of the founding committee Mohammed Seif al-Mazroui said on Monday the number of subscribers exceeded 120,000, WAM said.
The company said in June it was offering 27.5 million shares, or 55 percent of its authorised capital, at 10 dirhams each in the IPO open to United Arab Emirates nationals.
The IPO announcement said British Aerospace (BAe) had acquired a 13 percent stake in Oasis.
It said BAe was a strategic partner in the company, which will seek leasing deals in the oil-rich Gulf region.

The company said the founders -- including Abu Dhabi Investment Co, the Private Department of UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, three Abu Dhabi-based national insurance companies, Dubai Investment Co and 20 members of the ruling al-Nahayan family -- contributed 45 percent to the company's capital. ($1=3.67 dirhams)
